governance.attested_by: miso33 ct-committed-115 bit-ceil-097 2026-07-01 (probe on miso23 keeper; CT_PEAKER committed retune + BIT ceil fine-tune)
governance.note: Two offer-curve faithfulness levers on top of miso23 (all miso23/miso22/miso21 levers retained). (1) CT_PEAKER committed band lowered 1.55->1.15: restores the CT committed tranche to a physically-grounded level consistent with CAMPD part-load data for intermediate-split CTs. (2) COAL_BIT sigmoid passthrough ceil raised 0.95->0.97: narrows the BIT coal SRMC discount in dear-gas years from 5% to 3%, reflecting observed bidding where BIT offers approach SRMC as gas-coal arbitrage tightens. Both changes are physically grounded, NOT fit to the price or volume residual. RESULTS: CT_PEAKER committed 1.55->1.15 moved gmModel CT_PEAKER by <0.2 TWh/year — confirming the ~20 TWh/year CT under-dispatch is structural (missing reserve-demand co-optimization + zonal granularity), NOT addressable via offer curves. BIT ceil 0.95->0.97 marginally improved the 2025 coal-gas family balance (C2 gas improved from -11.6% to within tolerance at -1.9%). C3a 2023 still passes; 2024/2025 C3a unchanged.

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS requiring structural model improvements, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so the determination is honestly NOT-YET. MISSES: (1) C1 MERIT-ORDER SUBSTITUTION (the headline, UNCHANGED): model over-runs cheap CC_REGULAR (gmModel +47/+44/+33 TWh vs EIA-923 for 2023/24/25) and under-runs peakier CT_PEAKER (-21/-20/-21 TWh) and ST_GAS (-10/-14/-12 TWh). Run 33 CONFIRMED this is NOT offer-curve-addressable: CT committed 1.55->1.15 moved CT_PEAKER <0.2 TWh/year. Root causes: (a) single-node-per-zone topology eliminates within-zone congestion forcing local CT/ST dispatch, (b) MISO's ELMP reserve-demand co-optimization not modeled, (c) import deliverability gap (model under-imports by ~5-18 TWh vs actuals) lets domestic CC fill the shortfall. Next levers: reserve-demand co-optimization, intra-zonal congestion, import deliverability. (2) C2 2025 COAL OVER-RUN: coal +10.1% vs EIA-930 (211.4 vs 192.1 TWh). Coal take-or-pay + PRB sigmoid in dear-gas year ($3.52 HH) over-commits coal. Gas side now passes (-1.9%). (3) C3a PRICE LEVEL: 2024 -14.1%, 2025 -16.7%. Missing ELMP scarcity rents + no intra-zonal congestion + import gap depress model prices. 2023 passes. (4) C3c SCARCITY TAIL: 0 model >$200 hours vs 30/37/88 actual. MISO's ELMP/Reserve Demand Curve not modeled; the energy-only LP cannot produce scarcity spikes. (5) C5b STORAGE THROUGHPUT: 2025 +1307%. Nascent MISO battery fleet (~0.5 GW); model daily-cycling heuristic over-dispatches vs the incomplete EIA-930 signal. Small absolute volumes (0.13 vs 0.02 TWh). (6) C5c STORAGE SHAPE: 2025 r=0.40. Same root cause as C5b. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET — C1 (HARD) and C2 (HARD) fail with genuine model misses, no reclassification to caveat is appropriate.
